claims.statement: Every registered exact small-budget census has exact presentation-collapse, pair-collision, singleton, and multiplicity statistics that agree with an independent direct oracle.
claims.scope: Cumulative budgets (1,1), (2,1), (1,2), and (2,2) on the pinned three-word, six-step protected interface.
assumptions: The merged #966 enumerator and semantics are exactly pinned
Equivalence is equality of the complete registered observation table
falsifiers: Equivalent-pair count differs from direct pair scan
claims.strongest_parent: PR #966 reported 126 presentations and 18 classes but did not emit the full rate family over every registered budget.

claims.statement: A strictly positive exact-rational sum of protected-semantic Hamming, raw-resource L1, and development-history Levenshtein distances is a metric on the registered morphology product.
claims.scope: Complete three-case protected observations, resources bounded by (2,2), and legal histories of length at most four.
assumptions: Histories start at the registered seed and obey the declared transition law
dependencies: Standard Hamming, L1, and edit-distance metric properties
claims.strongest_parent: PR #966 defined a name-independent descriptor but explicitly left a validated distance open.
limits: No universal ontology or canonical metric weights

claims.statement: Nearest-archive morphology distance is syntax-free, vanishes exactly on archive morphologies, and is 1-Lipschitz in the query.
claims.scope: The four distinct (1,1) archive morphologies and all 576 registered (2,2)-budget presentations.
assumptions: Archive is finite, nonempty, and duplicate-free
Archive entries are morphology records rather than program texts
claims.strongest_parent: No parent supplied a semantic/resource/developmental nearest-archive novelty metric.
limits: No optimality claim for weights or threshold

claims.statement: Every certified operation-token remint preserves the complete registered morphology record and therefore all distances and novelty values.
claims.scope: All 5! token bijections on all 576 registered presentations.
assumptions: The matching inverse decoder is used
Protected semantics and raw resources are unchanged
falsifiers: A certified round trip changes a record
A semantics-changing decoder swap is incorrectly accepted
claims.strongest_parent: PR #966 proved descriptor remint invariance on 126 presentations; this tranche covers the full 576-record metric domain.
limits: Not invariance under non-isometric grammar redesign

claims.statement: The registered 1/100-per-coordinate weight perturbation changes every distance and archive novelty score by at most 9/100 and preserves all strict novelty orders and the 11/2 threshold labels.
claims.scope: Weights (5,3,2) and (501/100,299/100,201/100) on the bounded registered morphology domain.
assumptions: History edit distance is at most 4
falsifiers: Threshold label changes without entering the bound margin
claims.strongest_parent: No parent established an explicit metric-weight perturbation certificate for the Section-F morphology space.
limits: Only the explicitly bounded perturbation box
Tied orders are not asserted to become strict in a fixed direction
Metric stability is not clustering stability

open_gaps.reason: No scalable large-budget sampler is implemented.
No 10^8 generation or equivalent coverage proof is supplied.
Reachable fractions under each development/search law remain unmeasured.
No post-hoc cluster-to-family mapping is performed.
No UNKNOWN cluster class is exercised without a clustering study.
Metric stability is proved, but no cluster partition exists to validate.
General program equivalence remains outside the finite interface.
